prediction.likelyOutcome: 721 should prevail on liability -- CRD's handwritten assumption of Gibbs-period repair responsibility, corroborated by its own principal's trial testimony, is difficult for CRD to escape. The dollar outcome turns on whether the court treats the $106,077.89 full resurfacing as the reasonable cost of curing CRD's inadequate patch work or as a capital improvement beyond CRD's repair obligation; a partial recovery in the high-$50,000s to mid-$80,000s is the most likely result, with lost profits, fees, and interest as additional but currently unquantifiable upside.

issues.label: CRD's Contractual Assumption of Gibbs-Period Damage (Core Liability)
Lost Profits Under the S&P Parking Lease

outcome.description: After a one-day bench trial the court found CRD liable for damage during both leases and awarded 721 all of its claimed repair costs, $106,077.87 (no lost-profit award is described), then awarded $51,770.71 in attorney's fees and judicial interest. The Fourth Circuit affirmed liability but held Gibbs and CRD solidarily liable for the Gibbs-period damage, amended the judgment to reduce the damages by 50% for the settled co-obligor's virile share, and reversed the attorney's fee award because the lease did not provide fees for a Clause 13 breach.
outcome.finalNote: Reduced on appeal to a 50 percent share.
